page.layout: One printed page, one text column of full-width lines. Running head at the top centre, page number at the top right. The text opens with two catechism sections (questions in italic, answers in roman), then a rule, then the section "DE NOMINE." with its questions and answers. Bottom centre: gathering signature "a 2". No margin notes.

main_text.head: Unde fit Vox?
Quot sunt literæ, quibus Teutonica lin-gua scribitur?
Quotuplex est Vox?
Quot sunt voces Numeri?
DE NOMINE.
Quid est Nomen?
main_text.p: NOmen est vox numeri cum genere, casu & declinatione.
main_text.head: Quotuplex est Nomen?
Quid est Substantivum Nomen?
main_text.p: Cujus significatio per se absq; altero addito intelligitur: ut, Der Mensch/Homo, Der Vatter/Pater.
main_text.head: Quid est Adjectivum Nomen?
main_text.p: Cujus significatio absque altero intelligi non potest: ut, weiß/albus, schwarz, niger.
main_text.head: Quot sunt comparationis gradus, qui nonnullis Adjectivis accidunt?
main_text.p: Post positivum duo gradus nominantur, Compa-rativus & Superlativus.
main_text.head: Unde Comparativus & Superlativus formantur?
main_text.p: A positivo, cui addendum est er / pro comparativo, & ste vel este [?] pro superlativo: ut, flug/ fluger/ [?]

page.notes: The Fraktur letters in the alphabet list and the German examples are hard to read at this scan resolution; the letter forms and the Greek/Hebrew letter names at the end of the alphabet list are marked [?]. "este" in the comparative rule is uncertain, as is the final word "fluger/", which continues on the next page. The running head is set in capitals and is not repeated as a heading.
